baselines.purpose: Simple frozen comparison opponent for Arena; not a claim of competitive strength or general card understanding.
baselines.sourceAttribution: WindBot contributors; retained root MIT license
adaptations: Namespace and explicit factory selection; deck attribute removed. Original registered action order, handlers and instance state retained.
Uses the retained current shared DefaultExecutor callbacks and GameAI selection path; not a byte-identical historical engine.
Policy model and training options are rejected. Generic SKYNET remains the default.
baselines.qualityStatus: bounded static script and lifecycle review; ten focused assertions and two native completion fixtures passed
baselines.scriptReviewScope: Reviewed the eleven effect-bearing constants against these exact local Lua files. This checks prompt stages and lifecycle assumptions, not optimal play or every inherited DefaultExecutor path.
knownLimitations: OldSchool is a simple historical beatdown strategy, not a modern combo baseline.
Double Summon only activates when its original offered-summon and hand-count heuristic passes; it can miss opportunities after the ordinary summon has already been spent.
Gear Golem the Moving Fortress is set as a defender; its optional direct-attack effect is not registered.
Sweep-removal heuristics and inherited tied-destruction selection are coarse and are not optimal labels.
Historical deck is a research fixture; no modern format legality or banlist compliance is claimed.
Changing DeckFile does not make the expert understand unregistered cards.

arenaEvaluation.interpretation: A functioning, frozen evaluation baseline with a substantial card-coverage gap. The 20-match result is 2 candidate wins and 18 expert wins; the separate pilot is not pooled. This is not a promotion test, controlled paired-seed experiment, or proof of performance on other decks.

sharedEffectMigration.scriptArchiveRead: Only the four exact named Lua entries; 65536-byte metadata and actual-read limit per entry. No discovery outside configured paths.

expertOrigin.status: Historical local source is an inspiration only, not an optimal teacher or verified recent implementation.

26412047.effect: Destroy one faceup attack-position monster with global maximum current ATK across both players. No targeting.
26412047.choice: Only ties generate resolution HintMsg.Destroy; choose opponent from actual offered ties or lowest-value own unavoidable card if board changed.
26412047.limitations: Does not simulate responses, immunity, or destruction replacement.

43422537.effect: Set current-turn normal summon/set cap to 2, not add one to cap; no once-per-turn activation restriction.
43422537.choice: No card choice. Stateless policy requires two distinct currently offered level 1-4 hand developments and two empty main zones, scored before ordinary development.
43422537.limitations: Conservative partial support: excludes opportunities after first normal summon/set, tribute continuations, special summon-count mechanisms and restrictions after the first development.

72302403.effect: Normal Spell remains on field, flips facedown enemy monsters at resolution, prevents opponent attack declarations while its field effect applies, self-destructs after third opponent end phase.
72302403.choice: No card choice. Avoid duplicate active faceup copy; accept reveal or visible battle threat.
72302403.limitations: No forecast of future removal, re-enabling negated copy, piercing, attack effects or future enemy draws.

70342110.effect: On opponent attack declaration, automatically targets attacker; banishes at resolution if it remains related, attackable and attack not cancelled.
70342110.choice: No card choice or pending target queue. Observe current enemy attacker and UnderAttack; preserve defense-position attackers.
70342110.limitations: Own pending Prison target or Mirror Force is a conservation heuristic, not proof of outcome. No broad trap-immunity guard because inherited ImmuneTrapMonster means trap destruction immunity.

validation.nativeInterpretation: All ten duels completed with normal retirement. Logs confirm actual effect activation/resolution and tied Hammer selection; synthetic tests additionally cover mixed-side ties, changed identity, negated responses and pure probes. Fixtures deliberately favor their test condition; win/loss counts are not strength evidence. Both recorded host seats were exercised; opening-turn role was not forced. The first six duels used the effects-only binary; the final four used the same card behavior after the learning-provenance rebuild, as recorded by their hashes.

cleanup.evidence: Get-Process found no SKYNET/SKYNET_DUEL_HOST; Arena active-run API and live gateway rooms API returned empty lists. Stored first-run roomCount was 1 at completion, so final retirement is established by these independent live checks.

sharedEffectArenaEvaluation.interpretation: Exploratory single-deck comparisons, without tuning weights or policy after observing the runs. Updated SKYNET beat its preserved predecessor 18-2 and scored 9-11 against the preserved expert, compared with the historical 2-18 initial expert comparison. Samples are independent and unseeded, not paired. No trained checkpoint or automatic promotion; no claim of competitive general deck play.

sharedStrategyUpdates.scope: Shared Emergence, Mo Ye and Chixiao route, actual material/cost/search/negate prompts, and optional ranked-decision explanations. No complete modern executor or neural inference.

validation.nativeInterpretation: Six final-binary duels completed normally. Actual logs show Emergence search, Mo Ye reveal/token/draw, token/Wyrm Synchro materials, Chixiao search and negate with graveyard banish cost and enemy target. Trap Hole removes Mo Ye while its token effect resolves; subsequent offers abandon Chixiao until resources are restored. Host seats 0 and 1 exercised; not a strength benchmark. Two earlier exploratory Mo Ye duels are excluded from this final-binary receipt.

arenaEvaluation.comparison: New general policy vs preserved previous v2 general policy, identical compact Swordsoul deck, built-in weights and training disabled
arenaEvaluation.interpretation: Exploratory single-deck gain from newly supported cards against a predecessor lacking them; no competitive modern-expert benchmark, held-out generalization, paired RNG, trained checkpoint or automatic promotion.

limitations: Ranked-action explanations do not cover every battle/selection callback and are capped at 128 decisions per duel.
Full Swordsoul/Tenyi, Taia, Longyuan, Blackout and Emergence banished-level effects are unsupported.
Normal-summon planning estimates a reveal resource from visible own-hand categories; the actual core prompt proves reveal eligibility.
Policy v3 episodes must be collected fresh; existing compatible weights may initialize them but old episodes must not be relabeled.
